alignments.note: Substantival article before a participle with a single English word written for the pair: the article takes the relativizer-pronoun and the participle keeps its verb (rules 32, 90).

Participle with the object English requires it to repeat; a resumptive pronoun is a rule 7 helper on the verb licensing it (rule 103's contrast clause). Reading the second us as a discontinuous second realization of hemas remains defensible.
Adjective and noun both anarthrous, so the supplied determiner and the case preposition go with the noun, discontinuously (rules 58, 15).
Determiner slot displaced by the possessive belonging to hemon (rule 20).
idios is the source word the supplied possessive belongs to (rule 47); the Greek is anarthrous here, so nothing competes.
Noun; the ASV writes no determiner for it, so rule 31's postposed-determiner clause has nothing to place.

Attributive article governing the participle dotheisan behind the expressed head noun charin. Rule 31's test for a following participle is whether the article governs an expressed head noun: it does, as in ten dynamin ten energoumenen -> the power that worketh, so the article realizes nothing and the relativizer is the participle's helper. The postposed-article clause that gives which to the article is scoped to a prepositional-phrase modifier, which has no verb to carry a relativizer; that is the configuration at 1:1 and 1:13, not this one. 1:14 reads the identical shape the same way (rule 24).
Passive participle rendered as a finite relative clause; the supplied relativizer and copula are its rule 7/9 helpers, head on the lexical verb (rule 31).

review_notes: Corrected ten (s019): the accepted alignment gave it the supplied which under rule 31's postposed-article clause, but that clause is scoped to an article whose modifier is a prepositional phrase. Here the modifier is the participle dotheisan and the article governs the expressed head noun charin, which is rule 31's test for emptying it; which was given now stands whole on the participle headed on given. This also brings the verse into line with 1:14, where tou before enoikountos behind the expressed pneumatos is likewise unrepresented (rule 24).
No determiner question arises for charin: the ASV writes and grace with no article of its own, so rule 31's supplying clause has nothing to place on the noun.
The repeated us of called us was folded onto the participle as a rule 7 pronoun helper rather than marked added or joined to hemas.
A reference comparison will report the unrepresented ten as a disagreement; that report is not a correction.
